also: can’t tear myself away from (my books)

terms.gloss: be stuck, stick fast; be stuck for what to do
evidence: Plaut. Capt. 3.3.17: quid māchiner? quid comminīscar? haereō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin says it with the verb: haereō, I’m stuck. Also of a small child stuck on the shapes of the letters (haesit circā fōrmās litterārum, Quint. 1.1.21).

evidence: Ter. Phorm. 780: in eōdem lutō haesitās
terms.comment: Rare in this literal sense, and not in Cicero, who uses it for “hesitate”.

phrases.latin: tum vulpēcula ēvāsit puteō nīxa celsīs cornibus hircumque clausō līquit haerentem vadō
phrases.english: then the little fox climbed out of the well on his tall horns and left the goat stuck in the water

phrases.latin: ego stirpem ingentem, vestīgiō pedis ejus haerentem, revellī
phrases.english: I pulled out a huge thorn stuck in the sole of his foot

phrases.latin: obstipuī, steteruntque comae et vōx faucibus haesit
phrases.english: I froze, my hair stood on end, and my voice stuck in my throat
The ball’s stuck in the tree.
I can’t tear myself away from my books
I am quite stuck in my writing
